title: Operatorized control-plane provisioner: immutable deployments, automated health watchers, and graceful rolling upgrades
creator: Sanjay Iyer
description: Create a new Terraform module + companion K8s operator pattern for provisioning and lifecycle management of Redwood Private EKS control planes. Goals: 1) shift from mutable in-place terraform updates to an immutable, operator-driven rollout model for controlplane components; 2) provide preflight and continuous health checks (both infra and control-plane mesh) that fail fast before cutover; 3) implement canary+rolling upgrade strategy with automatic rollback hooks and clear observability; 4) make cross-account KMS usage and cluster CA rotation safe and auditable. This ticket covers module design, implementation scaffolding, CI pipelines, and an initial staged rollout for one internal customer environment.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module (sources/linear path) supports operator bootstrap and outputs required boot artifacts (S3 state path, IAM roles, KMS key alias, OIDC provider) for Private Control Plane installation.

A lightweight Kubernetes operator (declarative CRD) is documented and deployed during bootstrap to manage control-plane resources (core components, kube-apiserver config, controlplane-nodes ASG/managed nodegroups).
Upgrade process that performs canary rollout to a 'shadow' control plane followed by automated health checks and progressive traffic shift is implemented and tested in staging.

Preflight checks run as part of terraform plan/apply pipeline: VPC reachability, subnet ENI capacity, KMS cross-account policy, IAM role trust boundary, and existing CA cert validity — failures surface actionable errors.

Health watchers emit metrics/events to Console: controlplane_ready, api_latency_p95, etcd_mvcc_db_total_size, kubeapi_unauth_errors and are wired to the rollout controller to trigger rollback on defined thresholds.
Runbooks and rollback playbook are added to Confluence with links in ticket.
Security review completed for KMS usage and operator RBAC and documented in ticket metadata.
notes: Design iterated after infra charter meeting (2025-02-25). Decided to avoid changing customer-facing API shape in this iteration; operator is internal infra component managed by Redwood ops SDK. Chose immutable pattern to reduce dependency drift and provide safe canaries for control-plane upgrades (less blast radius). Implementation will use EKS managed nodegroups only for control-plane-adjacent tooling; control plane itself remains EKS managed but we install a small operator on the customer VPC to coordinate safe cutovers and S3-backed state references. Key trade-offs: increased bootstrap complexity vs much lower upgrade risk. We will measure time-to-upgrade and rollback rate during rollout window.
design_decisions: Operator pattern selected over pure terraform because we need continuous, in-cluster health watchers and progressive traffic shifting that Terraform cannot express safely.
Use immutable resource naming (timestamped resources) for controlplane-related infra so rollback can be achieved by shifting route53 / LB targets rather than in-place edits.
Keep control plane cert rotation out of scope for initial rollout; create separate follow-up ticket to automate root CA rotation across standby control planes.
Prefer KMS alias per-customer with least-privilege grants and an allow-list for cross-account decrypt roles.
implementation_plan: 1) Create terraform module 'rwd_priv_controlplane_operator' with outputs consumed by operator installer. 2) Implement operator repo skeleton (Go controller-runtime) that watches CRs and performs staged provisioning using the terraform operator or calling the module via runner. 3) Add preflight checks as a terratest suite and a lightweight preflight binary that runs in CI. 4) Wire metrics to existing Console observability endpoints and add dashboard templates. 5) Create CI pipelines: module plan/apply gated by preflight success, operator image build + canary deploy to staging cluster, integration test against staging control plane. 6) Draft runbook and add feature flag for internal gradual rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for terraform module (tfsec, checkov), terratest for preflight checks, integration test that exercises canary upgrade flow in staging (deploy new controlplane revision, validate health watchers, shift traffic, verify rollback triggers). Add load test to simulate api-server spike to ensure rollback threshold protects downstream systems.
risks: Complexity of cross-account KMS policies causing bootstrap failure
Operator RBAC mistakes could leak privileges if not scoped
Rollback windows may cause transient API errors for customers; require careful communication and scheduled maintenance windows
mitigations: Create a KMS policy generator and automated lint step in CI
Scoped service account and OPA policy enforcement for operator actions
Add circuit-breaker that pauses rollouts if dependent services are degraded; require manual approval for high-risk customers

manual_steps: 1) Run ./scripts/preflight.sh -e staging to validate env. 2) terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=staging.tfvars. 3) Deploy operator image to staging via images/redwood/controlplane-operator:canary. 4) Trigger CR apply to start canary controlplane build. 5) Observe metrics and follow runbook for rollback if thresholds crossed.
estimated_cost_impact: expected +15% infra during canary window for duplicated control plane resources; long-term lower incident cost and reduced rollback time.
